message.content:
Here’s a quick roundup of some of the most highly regarded crime‑thriller films released in 2020:

| # | Title | Director | Notable Cast | Why It Stands Out |
|---|-------|----------|--------------|-------------------|
| 1 | **The Invisible Man** (2017) – *Note: Released in 2020 in many markets* | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern twist on the classic horror tale, blending psychological suspense with social media paranoia. |
| 2 | **The Gentlemen** | Guy Ritchie | Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam, Hugh Grant | Ritchie's signature fast‑paced dialogue and stylish heist plot make this a sharp, witty crime caper. |
| 3 | **The Irishman** | Martin Scorsese | Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci | Though a 2019 release, it saw wide theatrical runs in 2020; its epic scope and deep character study earned critical acclaim. |
| 4 | **Uncut Gems** | Josh & Benny Safdie | Adam Sandler, Kevin Garnett | Sandler’s manic performance and relentless pacing create an adrenaline‑filled narrative about risk and obsession. |
| 5 | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | Ewan McGregor, Sacha Baron Cohen | A courtroom drama that blends historical events with sharp, witty dialogue, capturing the tension of political dissent. |
| 6 | **The Hunt** | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau | A tense, character‑driven story about a man accused of a crime he didn’t commit, exploring themes of guilt and redemption. |
| 7 | **The Nightingale** | Jennifer Kent | Lily Sullivan, David Wenham | A gritty, atmospheric film that follows a woman’s quest for vengeance in colonial Australia, blending historical context with visceral storytelling. |
| 8 | **The Last Duel** | Ridley Scott | Matt Damon, Adam Driver, Jodie Comer | A medieval duel turned crime thriller, featuring strong performances and a compelling exploration of truth and justice. |
| 9 | **The Devil All the Time** | Antonio Campos | Tom Holland, Ethan Hawke, Riley Keough | A bleak, atmospheric tale of violence and morality in rural America, with a strong ensemble cast delivering intense performances. |
|10 | **The Little Things** | John Lee Hancock | Denzel Washington, Rami Malek, Jared Leto | A slow‑burn procedural that builds tension through character dynamics and a haunting sense of dread. |

These films were praised for their direction, performances, and ability to keep audiences on edge—making them standout entries in the crime‑thriller genre during 2020.
